name: Claude Duet

description: Claude Duet is a new app from Anthropic where Claude works as a proactive agent, opened as a research preview on October 21, 2026. Built around Claude Opus 5.5, it sends a short morning brief from your connected apps, checks them every few hours, and messages you only when something needs attention. It runs on its own cloud computer with a browser, so tasks keep going when your devices are off, and it can use the 6,000 plus connectors in the Claude Marketplace. It shows you exactly what it will do and waits for approval before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything. Available on iOS, Android, and claude.ai by waitlist.

It generates explorable 3D scenes in about one second, turns a single image into an animation-ready 3D character with no separate rigging or skinning step, and creates full-body motion from text or video. Scenes are decoded into 3D Gaussian splats that play back in the browser. It is free to try in Viggle's PINOC app and available through the Viggle API and the PINOC MCP server.
bestFor: 3D scenes and worlds from a prompt

name: Recursive Flint
tagline: Open local coding model that runs fast on a laptop
description: Flint is Recursive's first model, released October 21, 2026: a mixture-of-experts coding model with 40 billion total parameters and about 2.5 billion active per token, built for agentic coding on local hardware. Recursive says it leads MoE models under 50 billion parameters on SWE-Bench Pro v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and SWE-Bench Verified (74.2%), and generates more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro. Weights are on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0 and work with llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and SGLang, plus Recursive's own rec engine. The model was built largely with Recursive's automated research system.
bestFor: private offline coding on your own machine
local coding agents in OpenCode or pi
fixing bugs and writing tests without API fees

It is built for latency-sensitive work such as browser agents, real-time search, voice and chat support, and tutoring, and it is available through an OpenAI-compatible API on the Inception platform, OpenRouter, Baseten, and Vercel AI Gateway.

A voice agent SDK built on LiveKit combines listening, reasoning, tool calling, and speaking in one streaming pipeline, over SIP or WebRTC. It runs on Mistral's EU, US, or global API or on your own infrastructure.
pricingNote: API from $0.0035 per minute for transcription; TTS $13 per 1M characters; voice agent API from $0.04 per minute

name: IBM Granite Speech 5.0

description: Granite Speech 5.0 is IBM's latest open speech collection, released October 21, 2026. The new granite-speech-5.0-2b model transcribes English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, translates to and from English, supports keyword lists of up to 2,000 terms, and ranks second among open-weight models on the Open ASR Leaderboard's average English word error rate. The updated 470M Turbo CTC model adds multilingual transcription with native punctuation and runs about 1.6 times faster than before, and the refreshed 4.1 2B Plus model improves speaker attribution and timestamps for meetings and calls. All are Apache 2.0.
pricingNote: Free open weights (Apache 2.0) on Hugging Face
